acceptance_mechanics.note: In fit_patient the first-round screen and the final acceptance share the same MAP objective when screening_metric == objective_metric == 'map'; the pattern search is monotone (best_cost never increases), so once the first round clears the 5% screen the final relative reduction is >= the first-round reduction and the final acceptance test cannot roll back. The only other rollback path is eq_correlation_rollback (|E-q Laplace correlation| >= 0.85), which with lock_ratio=True also flips refinement_accepted.

prior_width_scale_evidence.status: corrected 2026-10-12 (previous entry 2.0 was the current driver default, not the audit setting)
prior_width_scale_evidence.method: bitwise comparison of the 18 locked scenes (results/ct_reviewer_drivers_v6/paired_scene_ids.json) between this audit's records.jsonl and the width-1 and width-2 18-scene pilot arms run with experiments/run_screened_fem_locked.py --cohort ct120 --screen-threshold 0.05 --probe-count 2 --max-nfev 48
prior_width_scale_evidence.conclusion: The 120-scene official-prior audit used prior-width multiplier 1 (learned log-SD, floor 0.03). Its 73/120 acceptance therefore cannot be attributed to a width-2 prior; it reflects the ratio lock (two active parameters, five first-round evaluations), the 48-evaluation budget, and the CT observation regime. Acceptance rates are protocol-specific (synthetic primary 4/50 at width 1 / 96 evaluations / unlocked ratio; six-arm 26/50 at width 2 / 48 / contrast lock; CT120 73/120 at width 1 / 48 / ratio locked in all scenes) and are not comparable across protocols.
